title: INT8 GEMM: reduce conversion overhead + fuse dequant into epilogue; add correctness coverage
author: Grace Kim
release_notes:
- INT8 path: lower per-token overhead by removing redundant dtype conversions in GEMM hotpath and fusing dequant into GEMM epilogue where supported.
- Adds targeted INT8 correctness tests and expanded shape coverage for common decode/prefill configurations.
body: Motivation: In the FP8/INT8 benchmarking sprint we observed INT8 decode runs paying a non-trivial overhead in (a) repeated int8->fp16/bf16 conversions around GEMM boundaries and (b) a separate dequant kernel/loop after GEMM. This PR reduces that overhead by fusing dequantization into the GEMM epilogue when possible and by tightening the INT8 dataflow to avoid transient FP16 buffers in the decode loop. Summary of changes: (1) Adds a fused INT8 GEMM epilogue that applies per-channel scale (and optional zero-point) to the INT32 accumulators and writes FP16/BF16 output directly (no standalone dequant kernel). (2) Avoids redundant layout and dtype conversions in the decode hot path by reusing packed INT8 weights across steps and by caching per-layer quant params in a compact runtime structure. (3) Adds correctness coverage: unit tests for epilogue math (scale/zero-point handling), golden comparisons against FP16 for a small prompt set at multiple shapes (prefill + decode), and regression tests for previously flaky shapes seen in the benchmark lab. Performance notes (perf-lab, pinned clocks, batch=1/streaming decode unless otherwise stated): A100-80G: -6.8% TPOT (median) on Llama-family INT8 decode shapes (bs=1, seq=1 step), H100-80G: -4.1% TPOT median, L40S: -3.5% TPOT median; prefill improvements are smaller (~0-2%) due to being less conversion-bound. Limitations / fallbacks: We only enable fused epilogue when (a) group/per-channel scale layout matches our expected packing, (b) output dtype is FP16/BF16, and (c) accumulator path is INT32. Otherwise we fall back to the existing INT8 GEMM + dequant path. Correctness tolerances: For the unit tests we assert max_abs_err and relative error bounds aligned with our current quant guardrails; we also added a drift summary print in the test logs to ease triage if a future kernel change moves numerical behavior. Risk: Moderate. This touches a hot path in decode. Guarded behind runtime capability detection plus a config knob (default ON for supported GPUs once canary is green). Rollout: Land behind default-enabled path for A100/H100/H200, keep L40S enabled but monitor (L40S has shown intermittent correctness issues in other fused ops; this PR does not touch that fused op, but we will watch canary). References: ENG-24810 (sprint umbrella), ENG-24819 (INT8 guardrail), profiling notes in sprint working doc. Testing: unit tests added/expanded, ran microbench locally on A100 + H100, ran benchmark-lab quick matrix for top hosted decode shapes.
commits: kernels/int8: add fused dequant epilogue for int8xint8->int32 gemm
runtime/quant: cache quant params + reuse packed weights in decode loop
runtime/dispatch: gate fused epilogue by capability + param layout
tests: add INT8 epilogue correctness + shape regression cases
bench: add microbench for fused vs unfused INT8 GEMM (local only hook)
conversation: Hiro Tanaka (review): Can we be explicit about when the fused epilogue is enabled? I want to avoid silently changing numerics on unsupported packing layouts.

Grace Kim (author): Added a single gating function in int8_gemm_dispatch.cc and documented the three conditions in docs/internal/quant/int8-gemm-fused-dequant.md. Also added a debug log (guarded behind RWD_QUANT_DEBUG) that prints the chosen epilogue path + scale layout.
Noah Patel (review): Perf looks good. Concern: do we still allocate the FP16 staging buffer anywhere in decode? That allocation overhead was showing up in profiles.

Grace Kim (author): Removed the staging buffer on the fused path; for the fallback path it still exists but is now allocated once per layer and reused across steps (QuantParamsCache now owns the scratch). Added a small regression test that asserts no per-step realloc in decode loop when fused is enabled.

Yuki Sato (review): Please add coverage for the shape that triggered the auto-selector mismatch last week (m=1, n=11008-ish, k=4096 with odd alignment). Even if this PR doesn’t touch selection, it’s a good guardrail.
Grace Kim (author): Added test case 'decode_odd_n_alignment_smoke' and ensured fused epilogue disables itself for that shape until we finish alignment handling (falls back to unfused).
Priyanka Bose (review): For correctness tests, can we report a drift summary rather than a hard fail only? Helps compare changes across kernels.
Grace Kim (author): Added drift summary output (max_abs_err, p99_abs_err, relative) to the test logs; still fails on threshold violations. Thresholds match our current CI guardrail settings for INT8.
Connor O'Brien (comment): For release train, please keep this behind a knob and ensure perf-canary has coverage. We can default-enable after 48h green canary.

Grace Kim (author): Confirmed: fused path is controlled by runtime flag rwd.quant.int8_fused_epilogue (default true only when capability check passes). Canary integration is tracked in ENG-24817; this PR just provides the knob + logging.
Hiro Tanaka (approval): Approved. Please squash-merge and include perf numbers in the unreleased changelog entry.
Grace Kim (author): Done; updated CHANGELOG.unreleased.md with A100/H100 deltas and noted fallback conditions.
